paragraphs.text: And Rehoboam his son reigned in his stead. [31]

The book closed its account of Solomon without mentioning his falls in his love for foreign women and his turning aside to the worship of idols through them. This is because his kingdom is a symbol of the Kingdom of Christ, which must be holy and without sin, shining with the splendor of the Sun of Righteousness.
Let me meet You and possess You, O Wisdom of God!
v The queen of Sheba set out to Solomon, since she had heard of him.
And behold, You, the Lord of Solomon, have come down to me.
The queen of Sheba heard of the wisdom of Solomon, and carried gifts to him!
But You call me to be united with You, and to enjoy the fellowship of Your glory.
v Allow me to reveal to You all that is in my heart.
By Your Holy Spirit I sit at Your feet.
There I commune with You, O Bridegroom of my soul.
I hear Your voice, and enjoy Your splendor.
My heart melts in love for You.
And I long that all humanity be drawn to You.
v The queen of Sheba met those who worked in Solomon's palace.
She was dazzled by the management of his palace, and blessed those who worked with him and heard him.
But You open to me the doors of Your heavens.
I bless the prophets and apostles and disciples and all the believers.
And I long to praise You with them, as with all the heavenly orders.
I see in Paradise thieves who have become saints.
And I feel Your grace which has made those of the dust almost heavenly.
I stand in amazement before the riches of Your surpassing grace!
v The queen of Sheba counted all those around You the happiest of those on earth.
And behold, I see Your Church, the unique bride.
She bears the reflection of Your splendor, O You who are fairer than the children of men!
By Your light You have removed from her all darkness.
And by Your grace she has come to bear Your righteousness.
By Your cross she has become the queen sitting at Your right hand!
v Her dwelling has become with You in heaven.
Where the lion who longs to devour her cannot creep in to her!
The enemy will find nothing of his in her!
You are her light and her glory and her riches and her happiness.
You are everything, so she lacks nothing.
v Grant me to cling to You and possess You.
I will not leave You, but You dwell in me and I in You.
To You be glory, O power of God and wisdom of God.
In You I experience the earnest of Your heavens.
In You my heart and my mind are lifted up as to heaven.
In You I live happily whatever troubles of the world may come!
You lift me from glory to glory!

entries.section: 1. The folly of Rehoboam

paragraphs.text: And Rehoboam went to Shechem: for to Shechem were all Israel come to make him king. [1]
Rehoboam is the only son of Solomon whom history records, and he was born to Solomon of Naamah the Ammonitess (1 Kgs 14:31), who may have been the daughter of Hanun, king of Ammon.

“Rehoboam” means “the enlargement of the people,” and he was so called in remembrance of the completion of the acquisition of the Promised Land, which was not possessed fully until the last days of David (Ex 34:24). It is said of him that because of his lack of wisdom the kingdom was divided.

Some see that Solomon spoke of himself when he said: [He that begetteth a fool doeth it to his sorrow: and the father of a fool hath no joy] (Prov 17:21). For his soul became embittered in his last days when he realized that he would leave his kingdom to a son who lacked understanding. He expressed this by saying: [Yea, I hated all my labour which I had taken under the sun: because I should leave it unto the man that shall be after me. And who knoweth whether he shall be a wise man or a fool? yet shall he have rule over all my labour wherein I have laboured, and wherein I have shewed myself wise under the sun. This is also vanity... For there is a man whose labour is in wisdom, and in knowledge, and in equity; yet to a man that hath not laboured therein shall he leave it for his portion. This also is vanity and a great evil] (Eccl 2:18-19, 21).

entries.section: 1. The folly of Rehoboam

paragraphs.text: The wise man does not know what his heirs will do with what he labored for and acquired, but the one who is bound to heavenly wisdom in his life and conduct leaves them an inheritance of blessing that is not lost. What did the priest Zacharias and Elizabeth bequeath to St. John the Baptist? Their constant holy prayers and their righteousness in the Lord. Their life was a support to him in the wilderness while he was deprived of their visible care! 1. With Solomon's wisdom and his capabilities and sincere intention, he turned aside by his marriage to idolatrous women, and part of the fruit of this was that his son did not walk in the mind of his father. 2. Solomon erred in his excess in building projects and in spending on his wives, so he burdened his people with taxes, and this was a basic factor in the division of the kingdom. 3. Some see in these murmurers that they forgot what Solomon had done, for the kingdom lived forty years in peace and prosperity without wars, and his age was marked by prosperity for all. 4. Here the fault is shared: the people murmured and forgot the blessings of Solomon's age, and on the other hand Rehoboam put on his father's crown but did not enjoy his mind and wisdom. Nor did he enjoy the spirit of sincere shepherding that his grandfather David had. Rehoboam did not heed the wisdom of Job and his humility, for he said that he did not despise the cause of his manservant or of his maidservant when they contended with him (Job 31:13). The people needed gentle words from Rehoboam, and then they would be his servants for ever with all gladness [7]. For kind words cost us only a little self-denial, and by them we gain countless blessings.
Shechem All Israel gathered at Shechem to make Rehoboam the son of Solomon king over them.

Shechem lies about 40 miles north of Jerusalem, and it is a fitting center for such an important gathering, for it lies in the territory of Manasseh, and this pleased the people who lived in the north. In Shechem is the tomb of Joseph (Josh 24:32). Abraham, the father of all the Jews, was in Shechem (Gen 12:6), and also Jacob (Gen 33:18). And Joshua with all the tribes of Israel renewed the covenant with God in Shechem (Josh 24).
So the choice of Shechem carried the possibility of planting the spirit of unity between the north and the south, but sadly Rehoboam's conduct caused a grave schism and the division of the kingdom.

It was good that the gathering took place in Shechem, but sadly we do not hear of a renewal of the covenant with God, as happened when Saul became king, and also David (2 Sam 2:4) and Solomon (1 Kgs 1:28-30).
If we may say so, when Rehoboam received the kingdom God was not first in his heart, and he did not feel that he had received this work from His hands.

entries.section: 2. The extremism of the divided

paragraphs.text: 2 And it came to pass, when Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who was in Egypt, whither he had fled from the presence of Solomon the king, heard it, that Jeroboam returned out of Egypt. 3 And they sent and called him. So Jeroboam and all Israel came and spake to Rehoboam, saying, 4 “Thy father made our yoke grievous: now therefore ease thou somewhat the grievous servitude of thy father, and his heavy yoke that he put upon us, and we will serve thee.” 5 And he said unto them, “Come again unto me after three days.” And the people departed. 6 And king Rehoboam took counsel with the old men that had stood before Solomon his father while he yet lived, saying, “What counsel give ye me to return answer to this people?” 7 And they spake unto him, saying, “If thou be kind to this people, and please them, and speak good words to them, they will be thy servants for ever.” 8 But he forsook the counsel which the old men gave him, and took counsel with the young men that were brought up with him, that stood before him. 9 And he said unto them, “What advice give ye that we may return answer to this people, which have spoken to me, saying, Ease somewhat the yoke that thy father did put upon us?” 10 And the young men that were brought up with him spake unto him, saying, “Thus shalt thou answer the people that spake unto thee, saying, Thy father made our yoke heavy, but make thou it somewhat lighter for us; thus shalt thou say unto them, My little finger shall be thicker than my father's loins. 11 For whereas my father put a heavy yoke upon you, I will put more to your yoke: my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.” 12 So Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam on the third day, as the king bade, saying, “Come again to me on the third day.” 13 And the king answered them roughly; and king Rehoboam forsook the counsel of the old men, 14 And answered them after the advice of the young men, saying, “My father made your yoke heavy, but I will add thereto: my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.” 15 So the king hearkened not unto the people: for the cause was of God, that the LORD might perform his word, which he spake by the hand of Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam the son of Nebat.
And it came to pass, when Jeroboam the son of Nebat heard it, (who was in Egypt, whither he had fled from the presence of Solomon the king)
That Jeroboam returned out of Egypt. [2]

entries.section: 2. The extremism of the divided

paragraphs.text: And they sent and called him. So Jeroboam and all Israel came and spake to Rehoboam, saying, [3]

entries.section: 2. The extremism of the divided

paragraphs.text: Thy father made our yoke grievous: now therefore ease thou somewhat the grievous servitude of thy father, and his heavy yoke that he put upon us, and we will serve thee. [4]
The people were groaning under the heavy yoke of Solomon, for he did not bear the spirit of his father David, who truly loved his people and gave himself for their service.

As for Solomon, he did not serve his people; what occupied him was the fulfillment of his projects and his desires, in which he went to excess. As for Rehoboam, listening to the groaning of the people did not concern him. Rehoboam did not understand the meaning of leadership, for he was not a good shepherd like his grandfather David.

Solomon divided the state, with regard to the responsibilities of work, into twelve districts (1 Kgs 4:7-19), and it seems that he excepted the tribe of Judah; it followed from this that when he conscripted officials for the work he exempted Judah from the work (1 Kgs 5:13-18). This is what the prophet Samuel had indicated beforehand when the people asked for a king to be set over them like all the nations. He warned them, saying: “This will be the manner of the king that shall reign over you: He will take your sons, and appoint them for himself, for his chariots, and to be his horsemen... And he will appoint him captains over thousands, and captains over fifties; and will set them to ear his ground, and to reap his harvest... and ye shall be his servants” (1 Sam 8:11-18).

v There are indeed many other things able to give us boldness before God, and to show us radiant and approved, but most of all that which brings a good will from above is tender care for our neighbor, which Christ required of Peter[1].

St. John Chrysostom v We read of cases that are not unique, even with regard to kings, of how effective kindness (“love”) is, and how harmful are pride and rebellious words, since they led to the shaking and destruction of kingdoms.

v How many murmurings did the people direct against Moses, and yet he bore them! And when the Lord wanted to take vengeance for him on them, he preferred to offer himself to death in order to save them from the divine wrath (Ex 32:32).
With what tenderness Moses spoke with the people, even after they had sinned against him! He comforted them by his works, and consoled and encouraged them by his prophecy of the future.
Although he spoke with God much, yet when he spoke with the people he spoke gently and with joy.

v Moses was qualified to become above all men, so that they could not look upon his face (Ex 34:30). And he captivated them, so that they loved him because of his tenderness more than their admiration for the miracles that were done by his hands.
v David also followed in the steps of Moses, for when he was chosen to rule the people, he was gentle and compassionate, contrite in spirit, persevering, ready to show affection.
For before he sat on the throne he offered himself to destruction for all (1 Sam 17:22), and when he became king he made himself equal to all in war, sharing the work with them.
He was encouraging in battles, gentle in judgment (among the people), patient in bearing insults, more ready to bear with others than to return wrong for wrong. Therefore he was dear to all...
He loved the brave, even those who were his enemies, thinking that justice requires honoring those who endured much in war, as if they were men of his own army.

He admired Abner, the brave commander, although he was one of his adversaries; therefore he did not despise him when he asked him for peace but honored him, making a special feast for him (1 Kgs 2:5). And when he was killed by treachery, David grieved for him and lamented him...
It is no small thing for a king to show humility in his deeds, counting himself as the least of his people, refusing to eat or drink water that others had risked their lives to bring.

This David asked that God pour out His wrath upon him instead of its being poured out upon the people, offering himself to the destroying angel, saying: “Lo, I have sinned, and I have done wickedly: but these sheep, what have they done? let thine hand, I pray thee, be against me, and against my father's house” (2 Sam 24:17).

St. Ambrose v The good shepherd imitates the Chief Shepherd of shepherds, who said: Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends, so that he loves his neighbor more than himself.
The shepherd in name does not love his neighbor as himself, so he neglects him until the thief takes him or the wolf snatches him.
St. John Climacus

entries.section: 2. The extremism of the divided

paragraphs.text: And he said unto them, Come again unto me after three days. And the people departed. [5]

It was good that Rehoboam gave himself time to answer without haste, and good that he consulted the wise elders, but he erred because he did not seek the counsel of the Lord, and did not lift his heart to Him in prayer and the offering of sacrifices.

entries.section: 2. The extremism of the divided

paragraphs.text: And king Rehoboam took counsel with the old men that had stood before Solomon his father while he yet lived, saying, What counsel give ye me to return answer to this people? [6]

entries.section: 2. The extremism of the divided

paragraphs.text: And they spake unto him, saying, If thou be kind to this people, and please them, and speak good words to them, they will be thy servants for ever. [7]
The elders knew very well that the people were not rebelling against the king; they were ready to serve him with a good heart, if he were good and bore in his heart the spirit of sincere shepherding.
What occupied the heart of good leaders was that they were serving God Himself by their service and their self-giving for their people. They counted themselves servants, not men of authority.

The Word of God Himself came incarnate, not to be served but to serve and to give His life a ransom for many (Lk 22:24-27; Phil 2:1-13). He trained His disciples in leadership through service and the washing of the feet of those served (Jn 13:1-17), and He asked of us: “Whosoever will be great among you, let him be your minister; And whosoever will be chief among you, let him be your servant” (Mt 20:26-27).

v May he who is a ruler not be puffed up because of his work, lest he fall from the blessedness of humility, but it is fitting for him to know true humility as a service to many... May the greatest be as the least.

v It is fitting for those who occupy the chief positions to be ready to offer even bodily service, after the example of the Lord who washed the feet of His disciples. Therefore it was said, “(Let) the leader (be) as the servant[2]”.

St. Basil the Great v Keep faith and humility within yourself, for by them you find mercy and help, and hear divine words in your heart, and your guardian angel accompanies you outwardly and in secret.

v Humility is the garment of Godhead, for the incarnate Word clothed Himself with it, and spoke to us of it through our bodies. So everyone who puts it on truly imitates Him who came down from His height, and covered the virtue of His greatness with humility, and veiled His glory with it lest creation be burned by the sight of it.

v No one hates the humble, nor rebukes him, nor despises him, for his Master loves him. He loves everyone, and everyone loves him and longs for him everywhere, and wherever he is found they look at him as a luminous angel, and give him honor.
v Humility is a hidden power which the perfect saints obtain after the completion of their course, and grace gives this power only to those who are perfect in virtue[3].
St. Isaac the Syrian

entries.section: 2. The extremism of the divided

paragraphs.text: But he forsook the counsel which the old men gave him, and took counsel with the young men that were brought up with him, that stood before him [8]

His forsaking the counsel of the elders and consulting the young men was not in order to learn of another counsel and compare the two counsels, but he rejected the counsel of the elders because it was not according to his desire. For he did not want to serve, but to rule.

It is fitting for the servant to listen to the elders as to the young, looking at the whole community, with its elders and children and youths and women, as one family interacting together in the spirit of love and unity in humility before the Lord.

The Fathers of the Church speak to us of the need of the young for the elders, as of the elders for the young. The Apostle says: “Yea, all of you be subject one to another, and be clothed with humility: for God resisteth the proud, and giveth grace to the humble” (1 Pet 5:5).
The young Elisha began to work with the elder Elijah. St. Ambrose admires the joint work between the elder and the young servants, for each has a role that completes the other's.
v How beautiful is the unity between the elder and the young.
One bears witness, and the other gives rest.
One leads, and the other gives joy...
What of Elijah and Elisha? Although the Holy Bible did not say much about Elisha's being young, yet we can understand that he was the younger.
In the Acts of the Apostles, Barnabas took Mark with him, and Paul took Silas (Acts 15:39-40) and Timothy (Acts 16:3) and Titus (Titus 1:5).

We see also a division of duties among them. The elders lead, offering counsel, and the young show vitality of work. Most likely they were all alike in virtue, but not in years. They rejoice in their unity, as Peter and John did.

We read in the Gospel that John was young, by the testimony of his own words, and yet he was not inferior to the elders in merits and wisdom. He bears mature and dignified traits and prudence in his mind[4].
St. Ambrose

entries.section: 2. The extremism of the divided

paragraphs.text: And he said unto them (and asked them), What advice give ye that we may return answer to this people, which have spoken to me, saying,
Ease somewhat the yoke that thy father did put upon us? [9]

entries.section: 2. The extremism of the divided

paragraphs.text: And the young men that were brought up with him spake unto him, saying,
Thus shalt thou answer the people that spake unto thee, saying, Thy father made our yoke heavy, but make thou it somewhat lighter for us; thus shalt thou say unto them,
My little finger shall be thicker than my father's loins. [10]

Rehoboam did not heed the words of his father, wise in the Lord: “A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger. The tongue of the wise useth knowledge aright: but the mouth of fools poureth out foolishness” (Prov 15:1-2). Rehoboam did not realize the gravity of the tongue, for it is said: “There is that speaketh like the piercings of a sword: but the tongue of the wise is health” (Prov 12:18).

entries.section: 2. The extremism of the divided

paragraphs.text: For whereas my father put a heavy yoke upon you, I will put more to your yoke:
my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions. [11]

His words came violent and his tone harsh, so that instead of easing the yoke that his father had put on the people, even with a gentle word, he assured them that he would make it heavier, until he made it unbearable. He thought that by this he was exercising his right as a king with authority, indifferent to the welfare of the people and their feelings. He took a grave decision that shatters the unity of the kingdom, and shatters the personality of Rehoboam himself!
What David the righteous king had built, his grandson Rehoboam, in David's third generation, destroys.
Rehoboam erred in that he did not consult God, for he had no personal relationship with Him.
Scorpions: these are whips whose ends terminate in a pointed iron material, and their stroke resembles the sting of scorpions.

entries.section: 2. The extremism of the divided

paragraphs.text: So Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam on the third day, as the king bade, saying,
Come again to me on the third day. [12]

entries.section: 2. The extremism of the divided

paragraphs.text: And the king answered them roughly; and king Rehoboam forsook the counsel of the old men [13]

It is fitting for the leader not to meet the agitation of his subordinates with violence, lest he add oil to the fire, but rather to hold the wheel of leadership calmly and steadily through the storm until it passes in safety.

entries.section: 2. The extremism of the divided

paragraphs.text: And answered them after the advice of the young men, saying,
My father made your yoke heavy, but I will add thereto:
my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions. [14]

entries.section: 2. The extremism of the divided

paragraphs.text: So the king hearkened not unto the people: for the cause was of God, that the LORD might perform his word, which he spake by the hand of Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam the son of Nebat. [15]

If God, the Almighty, had declared beforehand through Ahijah the Shilonite what would happen [15], this does not justify Rehoboam's folly, nor lessen his responsibility for acting with arrogance and haughtiness, which the Lord used to carry out His purposes.

Often God permits the evil of fathers to be visited upon their children, if they walk in the same way as their fathers. Solomon left the Lord, so God permitted most of the people to leave Rehoboam the son of Solomon. God permits this to urge fathers who do not care about the troubles that come upon them to realize that what they do will return upon their children more than they imagine, for many are concerned that no harm should befall their children.

If God permitted the carrying out of His threats, so that the sin of Solomon was visited upon his son Rehoboam, at the same time He did not forget His promise to David, and therefore He kept two tribes for his grandson Rehoboam.

The Psalmist says in the Lord's words: “If they break my statutes, and keep not my commandments; Then will I visit their transgression with the rod, and their iniquity with stripes. Nevertheless my lovingkindness will I not utterly take from him, nor suffer my faithfulness to fail. My covenant will I not break, nor alter the thing that is gone out of my lips” (Ps 89:31-34).

entries.section: 3. Their rejection of Rehoboam

paragraphs.text: 16 And when all Israel saw that the king would not hearken unto them, the people answered the king, saying, “What portion have we in David? and we have none inheritance in the son of Jesse: every man to your tents, O Israel: and now, David, see to thine own house.” So all Israel went to their tents. 17 But as for the children of Israel that dwelt in the cities of Judah, Rehoboam reigned over them. 18 Then king Rehoboam sent Hadoram that was over the tribute; and the children of Israel stoned him with stones, that he died. But king Rehoboam made speed to get him up to his chariot, to flee to Jerusalem. 19 And Israel rebelled against the house of David unto this day.
And when all Israel saw that the king would not hearken unto them, the people answered the king, saying,
What portion have we in David!
And we have none inheritance in the son of Jesse!
Every man to your tents, O Israel.
And now, David, see to thine own house!
So all Israel went to their tents. [16]

Although it was Rehoboam who hardened his heart and acted without wisdom, the ten tribes counted their rebellion as not against Rehoboam but against David: “What portion have we in David? and we have none inheritance in the son of Jesse!” [16] And God counted this rejection as a rejection of His grace and His promises. So Judah became in God's eyes the representative of His people, and Israel was cut off from it.

Their evil appears from the following: 1. The great majority of the ten tribes accepted the worship of the calves. 2. They expelled the priests and the Levites, and appointed priests for the idols. 3. Those faithful to the faith went to Jerusalem and the cities of Judah.

entries.section: 3. Their rejection of Rehoboam

paragraphs.text: But as for the children of Israel that dwelt in the cities of Judah, Rehoboam reigned over them. [17]

entries.section: 3. Their rejection of Rehoboam

paragraphs.text: Then king Rehoboam sent Hadoram that was over the tribute; and the children of Israel stoned him with stones, that he died.
But king Rehoboam made speed to get him up to his chariot, to flee to Jerusalem [18]

Just as Rehoboam took the wrong counsel, so when he wanted to remedy his error he chose the wrong mediator. He chose Hadoram who was over the tribute, in whom they saw a representative of the heavy yoke that Solomon had put upon them. He did not send a man known for wisdom and gentleness whom they could listen to, but sent one whom they could not bear to see because of his position as general overseer of the forced labor.

entries.section: 3. Their rejection of Rehoboam

paragraphs.text: And Israel rebelled against the house of David unto this day. [19]
Take, O Lord, the wheel of leadership!
v In great Shechem Rehoboam met all Israel.
He received the throne of his father, marked by glory and riches.
He thought in himself that as a king he commands and is obeyed.
He did not hand the wheel of leadership over to You, nor did he renew the covenant with You and with Your people!
v He thought that all the people were slaves to him.
He did not imitate You, O King of kings, the Good Shepherd!
He did not imitate his grandfather David in the purity of his heart.
Nor did he hide himself in You, that You might work in him and through him!
v The people longed to see him truly as a grandson of David.
They asked him to lift from them the weight of the yoke that his father Solomon had put upon them.
They did not refuse to serve him, but asked him to be gentle with them, and then they would serve him faithfully.
v Rehoboam did not know to ask the Lord for counsel.
God was not the leader of his thought and his life.
He consulted the elders as well as the young.
He accepted the counsel that agreed with his desire.
In pride together with folly, violence found a place in his heart as in his mind.
v Grant me, O Lord, that You take the wheel of leadership.
Then I will walk by Your Spirit, O You who are all love and tenderness.
I long to be poured out for the sake of Your people.
And to find delight in serving all.
v Remove from my heart all harshness, and from my mouth every wounding word, that I may truly be Your ambassador!
v By violence the people lost their unity.
And schism and discord entered among them.
Grant me love and tenderness, that all may gather together to You.
Be the Leader of Your people, that in the spirit of unity all may go from strength to strength.
And all may experience true glory.
And all may walk in a delightful journey in Your company.
And all may set out as though to Your heavens!
To You be glory, O Leader, the Good Shepherd!

entries.section: 1. The attempt to recover the ten tribes

paragraphs.text: 1 And when Rehoboam was come to Jerusalem, he gathered of the house of Judah and Benjamin an hundred and fourscore thousand chosen men, which were warriors, to fight against Israel, that he might bring the kingdom again to Rehoboam. 2 But the word of the LORD came to Shemaiah the man of God, saying, 3 “Speak unto Rehoboam the son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all Israel in Judah and Benjamin, saying, 4 Thus saith the LORD, Ye shall not go up, nor fight against your brethren: return every man to his house: for this thing is done of me.” And they obeyed the words of the LORD, and returned from going against Jeroboam.

And when Rehoboam was come to Jerusalem, he gathered of the house of Judah and Benjamin an hundred and fourscore thousand chosen men, which were warriors, to fight against Israel, that he might bring the kingdom again to Rehoboam. [1]
Most likely Rehoboam gathered the warriors on the counsel of the young men who urged him to answer the people with violence, and so he lost the ten tribes by his violent words.

Rehoboam found justifications that moved him to desire to fight Jeroboam and the ten tribes, namely: 1. He looked on these tribes as schismatic and rebellious, needing to be disciplined. 2. As a lawful king from the house of David, he needed to affirm his authority and his military power to gather the twelve tribes together. 3. He was fulfilling the desire of his father Solomon the wise, who sought to kill Jeroboam because he lifted up his hand against him (1 Kgs 11:26, 40). Jeroboam fled to Egypt, and was there until the death of Solomon. Was not Solomon the wisest man on earth at that time? 4. The ten tribes killed Hadoram, whom he had sent to them for reconciliation, and in his view they had killed an innocent man of peace who had done no wrong (2 Chr 10:18). If David declared war on the Ammonites because they insulted his messengers (2 Sam 10:7), then Jeroboam killed the messenger of Rehoboam without cause. So in his view Jeroboam and the ten tribes needed to be disciplined.

entries.section: 1. The attempt to recover the ten tribes

paragraphs.text: But the word of the LORD came to Shemaiah the man of God. [2]

Rehoboam's repeated error was not returning to the Lord and consulting Him before acting. Therefore the Lord left him to accomplish what was in his mind, so he gathered a hundred and eighty thousand chosen men to fight the ten tribes; then He sent to him Shemaiah the man of God to reveal to him that he had wasted his time and effort in gathering this army, and that he must release them to return to their houses.

It was fitting for Rehoboam to consult the Lord in everything like his grandfather David, most of whose psalms affirm his trust in the counsel of the Lord and His power and care for him (2 Sam 2:1). He used to ask the Lord in every small and great matter, confident that He leads him to victory and grants him success in everything.
v “Deliver me, O LORD, from mine enemies: I flee unto thee.”
I who once fled from You, now flee to You.

For Adam fled from the face of God and hid among the trees of Paradise, so it was said of him in the Book of Job: “Like a servant who flees from the face of his master, and finds a shadow” (Job 7:2) LXX.
Woe to me, if I remain under the shadow, lest it be said afterward: [All those things pass away like a shadow] (Wis 5:9).
That you may fight the rulers of this world, of this darkness, the rulers of the wicked (the devil and his hosts).
Great is your striving, for you do not see your enemies and yet you overcome them![2]
St. Augustine v “And of thy mercy cut off mine enemies”: not because I am worthy of it, but for Your mercy's sake You free me from those who fight against me.
Deliver me from those who devise plots; grant me that You free me from distress.

“And destroy all them that afflict my soul: for I am thy servant.” Notice again how the request is fulfilled. It is not easily that we receive our requests, but we must make ourselves worthy of it, and contribute from our side what we must contribute, and so we present our requests.

(Bare) prayer is naturally not sufficient in itself. The Jews prayed, and the answer was: “When ye make many prayers, I will not hear” (Isa 1:15). Why do you wonder at this if (Ezekiel) himself was not heard? For it was said: [If Noah, Job and Daniel come, they shall not deliver their sons and daughters] (see Ezek 14:14).

entries.section: 1. The attempt to recover the ten tribes

paragraphs.text: That you may realize this, we do not only pray, but with prayer we make ourselves worthy to receive the blessings of the present and the future[3].
St. John Chrysostom v He who does not take refuge in the sons of men takes refuge in God, and everyone who takes refuge in God, He delivers from his enemies, visible and invisible.
Fr. Anthimus of Jerusalem

entries.section: 1. The attempt to recover the ten tribes

paragraphs.text: Speak unto Rehoboam the son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all Israel in Judah and Benjamin, saying, [3]

entries.section: 1. The attempt to recover the ten tribes

paragraphs.text: Thus saith the LORD, Ye shall not go up, nor fight against your brethren:
Return every man to his house: for this thing is done of me.
And they obeyed the words of the LORD, and returned from going against Jeroboam. [4]

When Rehoboam tried to bring the ten tribes back to his obedience, the word of the Lord came to him through Shemaiah the man of God: “Ye shall not go up, nor fight against your brethren: return every man to his house: for this thing is done of me” (2 Chr 11:4). They rejected David, so the Lord counted them as rejecting Him personally!
They deprived themselves of being counted the people of God, and not one good king arose from them.
Rehoboam set it in his heart to restore the unity of the people by force. But the Lord prevented him from entering into battle with the rest of the tribes, and indeed he stopped.

Why did God not permit Rehoboam to go to war against Jeroboam? 1. To punish Solomon for idolatry. 2. God permitted what happened to discipline Rehoboam, who did not consult the Lord before answering Jeroboam and those with him. 3. Because God separated the sheep from the goats so that Israel would not lead Judah astray. If the people were divided into two kingdoms, ten tribes under the name “the kingdom of Israel,” and two tribes under the name “the kingdom of Judah,” the Book of Chronicles, which is concerned with the Temple and worship, almost reckons that the kingdom of Israel, the northern kingdom that broke away from the house of David, does not exist. The king of Judah is considered the recognized one, being king of Judah and Benjamin and all of Israel who returned to Judah and Benjamin. At the same time the people of the schismatic kingdom are counted as brethren of the people of Judah and Benjamin, whom it is not lawful for them to fight, for they are still children of God, who seeks their salvation, not their destruction[4]. 3. That God might assure them that strength is not in the union of Judah with Israel, but in taking refuge in the Lord. 4. The Lord says, “Ye shall not fight against your brethren,” for it is not fitting for brethren under any circumstances to enter into battles together. When Abraham and Lot differed (Gen 12), Abraham reminded his nephew that it was not lawful for them to enter into a battle because they were brethren (Gen 13:8).

And when Jacob and Esau differed and entered into something like a battle that lasted all their lives, their descendants continued in bitter enmity for many centuries (Gen 27:41-46; Ps 137:7; Obad 10-13). And when David refused to kill Saul, who was doing all he could to kill David, the Lord rewarded him by handing him the throne and establishing his seat, and from his seed came the Messiah, the Savior of the world, and an intimate friendship formed between the two tribes of Judah and Benjamin after the death of David and Saul, and the two became one kingdom over against the other ten tribes.

It is fitting for the believer, in his longing for the salvation of all, not to do this out of blind fanaticism, but in love, through the sense of brotherhood and his awareness of the love of the holy God who gave His only-begotten Son for every person, and also his love for his fellow man. For the believer longs to be joined to all the children of men, those he knows and those he does not know, joined to his contemporaries and those who have departed and those who come after him. He is joined to them in the oneness of true love, in a spiritual kinship that rises above every bodily or blood tie. He is joined with them in the Head, “Jesus Christ,” and all are partners together in everything for ever, especially in holiness in the holy God.
v May we who have been made worthy of such mysteries show a life that is fitting for the gift, that is, show conduct of the utmost excellence!...

For whether a man is a father or a son or a brother or in any other kinship, he is not counted a true kinsman as when the kinship springs from heavenly relationships. What use is it to be bound by earthly family ties without being bound by spiritual ties?! What benefit is it if we are kinsmen on earth and strangers in heaven?! For the catechumen is a stranger to the believer, since he does not have the same Head spiritually, nor the same Father, nor the same city, nor the same food or garment or table or house, but is different from him.
These things belong to the catechumen on earth (that is, he is occupied with ordinary earthly matters), but the other seeks them (as heavenly things) in heaven.
One has Christ as King; the other's food is meats that perish and come to an end!
One has garments that the moth destroys; the other has the Lord of the angels!
One's city is heaven; the other's is earth!
So we have nothing in common; in what, then, is our fellowship?!
Are we twins, born from one womb?! For this is unable to establish a most perfect kinship.

entries.section: 1. The attempt to recover the ten tribes

paragraphs.text: Therefore let us strive to be citizens of the heavenly city![5]

St. John Chrysostom “And returned from going against Jeroboam”: Rehoboam responded to the words of the Lord by Shemaiah the man of God, perhaps because he feared failure, since he was not a trained military leader like David his grandfather, but was like his father Solomon, who had no strong military experience. And perhaps after he had built the strongholds and made sure of his military power, he entered into several battles after that against Jeroboam.
Moreover, on the other hand, he remained faithful in his worship of the Lord for three years, after which he turned aside to idolatrous worship.

entries.section: 2. Rehoboam's efforts to preserve the two tribes

paragraphs.text: 5 And Rehoboam dwelt in Jerusalem, and built cities for defence in Judah. 6 He built even Bethlehem, and Etam, and Tekoa, 7 And Bethzur, and Shoco, and Adullam, 8 And Gath, and Mareshah, and Ziph, 9 And Adoraim, and Lachish, and Azekah, 10 And Zorah, and Aijalon, and Hebron, which are in Judah and in Benjamin fenced cities. 11 And he fortified the strong holds, and put captains in them, and store of victual, and of oil and wine. 12 And in every several city he put shields and spears, and made them exceeding strong, having Judah and Benjamin on his side.
And Rehoboam dwelt in Jerusalem, and built cities for defence in Judah. [5]

Without doubt the division of the kingdom shook the image of Israel before the nations and peoples, yet Rehoboam did not care about the nations' mockery of them, but was concerned to fortify the borders of his state and many of the main cities in his kingdom. For in the age of his father Solomon, in the days of peace, there was no need to fortify them. Most of Solomon's work was building and development and production with trade.

entries.section: 2. Rehoboam's efforts to preserve the two tribes

paragraphs.text: He built even Bethlehem, and Etam, and Tekoa. [6]
He fortified Bethlehem, which is about ten kilometers from Jerusalem, famous as the birthplace of David and of the Son of David, Jesus Christ.
Modern excavations confirm the existence of fortifications for the cities mentioned here at that time[6].

Rehoboam was concerned to build fortresses in the east and west, and also toward the south, leaving the northern region like an open door, for two main reasons: 1. Rehoboam knew that Jeroboam was on good terms with Egypt, so he feared that Egypt would attack him from the south as a kind of alliance with Jeroboam, who had previously taken refuge in it when Solomon sought to kill him. 2. He left the north like an open door, for on the one hand the priests and Levites who were in the northern kingdom returned to him, where they had found resistance and the putting of priests of the idols and high places in their place. Some of the pious among the people also returned, who refused the worship of idols and wanted to worship the living God. Rehoboam hoped that the people would long to enjoy worship in Jerusalem, especially at the feasts and festivals.

entries.section: 2. Rehoboam's efforts to preserve the two tribes

paragraphs.text: And Bethzur, and Shoco, and Adullam. [7]

entries.section: 2. Rehoboam's efforts to preserve the two tribes

paragraphs.text: And Gath, and Mareshah, and Ziph. [8]
Gath: a city taken by the Jews from the Philistines in the days of Samuel and King David (1 Sam 7:14; 1 Chr 18:1).

entries.section: 2. Rehoboam's efforts to preserve the two tribes

paragraphs.text: And Adoraim, and Lachish, and Azekah. [9]

entries.section: 2. Rehoboam's efforts to preserve the two tribes

paragraphs.text: And Zorah, and Aijalon, and Hebron, which are in Judah and in Benjamin fenced cities. [10]

Hebron: it is Al-Khalil today and is mentioned often; Abraham, Isaac and Jacob dwelt in it, and Sarah, Abraham, Isaac, Rebekah, Leah and Jacob were buried in it. It was one of the cities of the priests and the cities of refuge, and David reigned in it seven years.

entries.section: 2. Rehoboam's efforts to preserve the two tribes

paragraphs.text: And he fortified the strong holds, and put captains in them, and store of victual, and of oil and wine. [11]

entries.section: 2. Rehoboam's efforts to preserve the two tribes

paragraphs.text: And in every several city he put shields and spears, and made them exceeding strong, having Judah and Benjamin on his side. [12]
Rehoboam built cities for defence in the south to face any attack from Egypt [5-12].

The fortified cities mentioned are toward the south and west, because he feared Egypt, but we saw the invader coming from Egypt, and the fortified cities did not stop him, for except the Lord keep the city, the watchman waketh but in vain.

entries.section: 3. The return of the priests and Levites

paragraphs.text: 13 And the priests and the Levites that were in all Israel resorted to him out of all their coasts. 14 For the Levites left their suburbs and their possession, and came to Judah and Jerusalem: for Jeroboam and his sons had cast them off from executing the priest's office unto the LORD: 15 And he ordained him priests for the high places, and for the devils, and for the calves which he had made. 16 And after them out of all the tribes of Israel such as set their hearts to seek the LORD God of Israel came to Jerusalem, to sacrifice unto the LORD God of their fathers. 17 So they strengthened the kingdom of Judah, and made Rehoboam the son of Solomon strong, three years: for three years they walked in the way of David and Solomon.

It is clear that these ten tribes resisted God by appointing priests for the high places and for the devils and the calves (2 Chr 11:15), and the priests of God and the Levites were compelled to leave the tribes and go to Judah and Jerusalem (2 Chr 11:14).
And the priests and the Levites that were in all Israel resorted to him out of all their coasts [13]

entries.section: 3. The return of the priests and Levites

paragraphs.text: For the Levites left their suburbs and their possession, and came to Judah and Jerusalem: for Jeroboam and his sons had cast them off from executing the priest's office unto the LORD [14]

entries.section: 3. The return of the priests and Levites

paragraphs.text: And he ordained him priests for the high places, and for the devils, and for the calves which he had made. [15]

The Book of Kings mentioned the worship of the calves, and here is a reference to another kind of idolatrous worship, whose adherents believed that demons or jinn took the form of goats and lived in desolate places. The origin of the Hebrew word for goats is the jinn. Primitive peoples used to worship what they feared. Sadly, we see here the people of God imitating these peoples and worshiping what they fear.

entries.section: 3. The return of the priests and Levites

paragraphs.text: When Jeroboam cast off the worship of the living God, and ordained for himself priests for the high places and the devils and the calves which he had made, he feared that the people would long to return to Jerusalem to worship in the Temple, so he permitted the priests and Levites to go to Jerusalem. They left their suburbs and their possessions, and Rehoboam was strengthened by their presence with the pious of Israel who were faithful in worship [17].
It is no wonder that he who rejected God also rejects His servants and longs to be rid of them.

At the same time it was to the benefit of these priests and Levites to leave Israel and go to the kingdom of Judah, where the Temple of the Lord and His altar are, and to be rid of the quarrels and vexations that the priests of the high places might stir up against them.
And we must not deny that Rehoboam and his people welcomed them, and did not feel that they were a burden on their kingdom after they had lost their suburbs and possessions and fields.
They fulfilled what the prophet Isaiah said afterward: “Open ye the gates, that the righteous nation which keepeth the truth may enter in” (Isa 26:2).

entries.section: 3. The return of the priests and Levites

paragraphs.text: And after them out of all the tribes of Israel such as set their hearts to seek the LORD God of Israel came to Jerusalem, to sacrifice unto the LORD God of their fathers. [16]

There were people in these tribes faithful to the Lord. When the priests and Levites went to Jerusalem, all the righteous and pious Israelites followed them, “such as set their hearts to seek the LORD God of Israel.” They left the inheritance of their fathers and went to dwell in Judah, that they might have full freedom to go to the altar of the Lord, and that they and their children might keep far from any enticement to the worship of goats.

These pious ones present a beautiful example for us: 1. They gave priority to the worship of God and care for the salvation of their souls and the souls of their children before any material benefit or temporal comfort and happiness. 2. They clung to the faithful priests of the Lord. It is written in Joshua: “When ye see the ark of the covenant of the LORD your God, and the priests the Levites bearing it, then ye shall remove from your place, and go after it” (Josh 3:3).

entries.section: 3. The return of the priests and Levites

paragraphs.text: So they strengthened the kingdom of Judah, and made Rehoboam the son of Solomon strong, three years: for three years they walked in the way of David and Solomon. [17]

The kingdom of Judah was strengthened, not only by the increase in numbers, nor by what they brought with them of their personal possessions, but the blessing of the Lord came upon the kingdom through their piety and their prayers and their clinging to the Lord.

entries.section: 4. The wives and children of Rehoboam

paragraphs.text: 18 And Rehoboam took him Mahalath the daughter of Jerimoth the son of David to wife, and Abihail the daughter of Eliab the son of Jesse; 19 Which bare him children; Jeush, and Shamariah, and Zaham. 20 And after her he took Maachah the daughter of Absalom; which bare him Abijah, and Attai, and Ziza, and Shelomith. 21 And Rehoboam loved Maachah the daughter of Absalom above all his wives and his concubines: (for he took eighteen wives, and threescore concubines; and begat twenty and eight sons, and threescore daughters.) 22 And Rehoboam made Abijah the son of Maachah the chief, to be ruler among his brethren: for he thought to make him king. 23 And he dealt wisely, and dispersed of all his children throughout all the countries of Judah and Benjamin, unto every fenced city: and he gave them victual in abundance. And he desired many wives.
And Rehoboam took him to wife
Mahalath the daughter of Jerimoth the son of David, and Abihail the daughter of Eliab the son of Jesse. [18]

Rehoboam was weak in indulging his pleasures, so he sought many wives as his father did. Yet he was wiser than his father, for it seems he did not take wives from the idolatrous women. One of them was of the descendants of Eliab the brother of David [18], another of the descendants of Absalom the son of David [20], and a third of Jerimoth the son of David [18].
The name of Jerimoth the son of David has not been mentioned before, and perhaps he was the son of one of David's concubines.

entries.section: 4. The wives and children of Rehoboam

paragraphs.text: Which bare him children; Jeush, and Shamariah, and Zaham [19]

entries.section: 4. The wives and children of Rehoboam

paragraphs.text: And after her he took Maachah the daughter of Absalom; which bare him Abijah, and Attai, and Ziza, and Shelomith. [20]

entries.section: 4. The wives and children of Rehoboam

paragraphs.text: And Rehoboam loved Maachah the daughter of Absalom above all his wives and his concubines: (for he took eighteen wives, and threescore concubines; and begat twenty and eight sons, and threescore daughters.) [21]
Rehoboam imitated his father in having many wives and concubines. And yet the book did not indicate that he imitated his father.

Of the sons of Solomon, only one person is mentioned, namely Rehoboam, and the rest were not worthy even to have their number mentioned. But as for the sons of Rehoboam, it mentioned their number: twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters.

entries.section: 4. The wives and children of Rehoboam

paragraphs.text: And Rehoboam made Abijah the son of Maachah the chief, to be ruler among his brethren: for he thought to make him king. [22]

entries.section: 4. The wives and children of Rehoboam

paragraphs.text: And he dealt wisely, and dispersed of all his children throughout all the countries of Judah and Benjamin, unto every fenced city: and he gave them victual in abundance.
And he desired many wives. [23]

Some see that Rehoboam acted wisely when he distributed the lands of Judah and Benjamin among all his sons, in order to avoid conspiracy against him as Adonijah and Absalom did, so that a schism would occur in the kingdom, so that they would be adversaries to their brother Abijah whom he made chief and ruler among them. On the other hand, as his sons were spread through all the cities, they would preserve the safety of the people and care for the cities he had fortified with walls and their storehouses, and would support their brother if a foreign invasion occurred, and he would also avoid the rise of any revolt in the country against Abijah.
Wonderful is Your love, O Holy One!
v Wonderful is Your love, and wonderful are Your dispensations, O my Savior!
For the salvation of the whole world You chose righteous Abraham!
You promised him that he would be a father of many nations!
And You chose Isaac his son and Jacob his grandson.
From his seed You raised up for Yourself a people, not out of partiality, but that You might come incarnate from his seed, and give Yourself as a redemption for all humanity.
v In its disobedience Israel turned aside, and rebelled against You, O Holy One.
From among the twelve, You set apart two tribes, Judah and Benjamin, and from them You established the kingdom of Judah, that perhaps they might walk in love and holiness.
You did not permit them to fight against the rebellious ten tribes.
For You seek brotherly love with holiness!
v Many turned aside, even from the two tribes, but You kept a holy remnant.
By Your wonderful dispensation You provided in every generation a holy remnant for Yourself!
From this remnant You were incarnate of the holy Mary for our redemption.
You seek that all humanity be sanctified and that love prevail in it.
Wonderful is Your love, O wonderful Holy One!
v Grant Your Church to be united with You always.
She walks in You, and is filled with love and holiness.
She becomes an icon of You, and is made worthy of the heavenly wedding.
The holy Father rejoices in her, and the heavenly orders marvel at her!
Give me a pure heart filled with love and holiness!

entries.section: 1. Ahaziah king of Judah

paragraphs.text: 1 And the inhabitants of Jerusalem made Ahaziah his youngest son king in his stead: for the band of men that came with the Arabians to the camp had slain all the eldest. So Ahaziah the son of Jehoram king of Judah reigned. 2 Forty and two years old was Ahaziah when he began to reign, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. His mother’s name also was Athaliah the daughter of Omri.
And the inhabitants of Jerusalem made Ahaziah his youngest son king in his stead: for the band of men that came with the Arabians to the camp had slain all the eldest.
So Ahaziah the son of Jehoram king of Judah reigned. [1]

From the words “the inhabitants of Jerusalem made Ahaziah…” we infer that the inhabitants of Jerusalem were probably not content with his taking the throne, perhaps because he was the youngest of his brothers or because of the weakness of his character, but they had no alternative, since the Arabians had slain all his brothers.
He became king only in outward form, for it was his mother who managed the affairs of the kingdom.

entries.section: 1. Ahaziah king of Judah

paragraphs.text: Forty and two years old was Ahaziah when he began to reign, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. His mother’s name also was Athaliah the daughter of Omri. [2]

The Septuagint says that Ahaziah’s age when he began to reign was twenty years. This is acceptable in light of what was said in the previous chapter, that Jehoram was thirty-two years old when he began to reign and reigned eight years, that is, he died at the age of forty; thus his son, who was twenty years old, had been born when his father was twenty. Ahaziah was influenced by the counsellors from the northern kingdom (Israel) more than any other king of Judah.

We read in the previous chapter of the captivity of the sons of Jehoram and his wives, but it did not say all his sons and all his wives. Therefore this chapter mentions one of his sons, “Ahaziah,” and one of his wives, “Athaliah,” who, together with her mother, the wicked Jezebel, may be said to have been a source of shame and disaster both for the kingdom of Israel and for the kingdom of Judah.
We have already seen how Athaliah wanted to destroy all the royal seed, in order to make sure that the divine promise concerning the continuance of David’s throne would not be fulfilled.

entries.section: 2. Ahaziah walks in the way of Ahab

paragraphs.text: 3 He also walked in the ways of the house of Ahab: for his mother was his counsellor to do wickedly. 4 Wherefore he did evil in the sight of the LORD like the house of Ahab: for they were his counsellors after the death of his father to his destruction.
He also walked in the ways of the house of Ahab: for his mother was his counsellor to do wickedly. [3]

After the burial of his wicked father Jehoram, the people were perhaps expecting the youngest son not to walk as his father had, but his mother and his family drove him to walk in the very same way as his father.
Ahaziah had no principles by which to live, but he trusted in his mother Athaliah the daughter of Omri, a woman of great ambition and extreme violence, who led him and counselled him to do evil.
Ahaziah made an alliance with Jehoram the son of Ahab.

entries.section: 2. Ahaziah walks in the way of Ahab

paragraphs.text: Wherefore he did evil in the sight of the LORD like the house of Ahab: for they were his counsellors after the death of his father to his destruction. [4]

entries.section: 3. Ahaziah joins Jehoram in the war

paragraphs.text: He walked also after their counsel, and went with Jehoram the son of Ahab king of Israel to war against Hazael king of Syria at Ramothgilead: and the Syrians smote Joram. [5]

entries.section: 4. Jehu kills Ahaziah

paragraphs.text: 6 And he returned to be healed in Jezreel because of the wounds which were given him at Ramah, when he fought with Hazael king of Syria. paragraphs.text: And the destruction of Ahaziah was of God by coming to Joram.
For when he was come, he went out with Jehoram against Jehu the son of Nimshi, whom the LORD had anointed to cut off the house of Ahab. [7]
We have previously spoken of Jehu in our commentary on the Second Book of Kings (2 Kgs 9:27-28).

What happened to Ahaziah is the fruit of clinging to evil friendships, associating with the wicked and intermarrying with them, and also of his worship of idols. If we do not fear being infected by turning aside to evil, then let us fear perishing with the wicked. Therefore the commandment came: [Come out of Babylon] (Rev 18:4).
