So the house of Ahaziah had no power to keep still the kingdom. [9]
Jehu killed Ahaziah, who had hidden in Samaria, thinking that he would be safe, and Jehu left Ahaziah’s body to be buried.

entries.section: 5. Athaliah, the mother of Ahaziah, seizes the throne

paragraphs.text: But when Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the seed royal of the house of Judah. [10]
This is recorded in (2 Kgs 11:1 etc.). Athaliah ordered the killing of her grandchildren in order to secure her remaining on the throne.

Athaliah was a wicked woman who sought to destroy the house of David forever, in order to set up a throne for herself on its ruins. She destroyed all the royal seed with brutality, and she probably wished to transfer the throne from the house of David to her relatives on her mother’s side.

The Holy Bible does not reveal her hidden motives and her plan, other than her securing that the throne would remain in her hand. The first to reflect on this matter was the historian Josephus, who described her actions as having inherited from her parents hatred for the house of David. He says of her that she wished “that no one of the house of David should remain alive, but that she should destroy the whole family, so that no king should afterwards take over afterwards, arising from the family [1].” Her motive was to prove false the divine promise that the seed of David would sit on the throne, and that the Messiah the Saviour would come from the seed of David.

Some see that, besides her desire that no one should touch her crown and that no one of the house of David should sit on the throne of Judah, Athaliah wanted to avenge the killing of Jezebel her mother and the destruction of her family at the hand of Jehu. She thought she was right to avenge her parents and her whole family even upon her own descendants, who were the successors of Jehoram of the house of David. Perhaps Athaliah had in the depths of her heart a bitter hatred for what had befallen her family; and her hatred for the house of David drove her to hate the God of David.

What Athaliah did was also practiced by Herod in the massacre of the children of Bethlehem, to keep the seat of the throne. Athaliah, and Herod also, thought that they had become secure, and did not realize that God is the Almighty and the Shepherd of His people.

God permitted what happened to the house of David to confirm that God’s care alone saved the situation, so that a small child of the house of David might remain, through whom a shining lamp would remain for the house, and from the seed of David the Messiah the Saviour would come. In vain the enemy of good tried to nullify God’s plan of salvation.

v I observed the wicked, and I saw them in peace. What peace? A temporary peace, changing, passing and earthly; and yet I also ask this of God. I saw those who did not serve God receiving what I desired, I who serve God, but my feet were almost gone, my steps had well nigh slipped (Ps 73:2). Now I understand why they have peace and refreshment on earth… because their punishment is not temporary, but fixed forever [2].
St. Augustine v Of the wicked after their death it is said: “Where is the tabernacle of the dwellingplaces of the wicked?”

If you consider this closely, can you deny that there is recompense from the divine justice? Happiness floods the heart of the first (the righteous), and misery the second. The first bears witness by his own soul that he is innocent of guilt, and the second is a criminal.
That man is happy in his departure from the world, and the other is grieved over.
Who can pronounce innocent one who is not innocent in the eyes of his own conscience? He says: [Where is the covering of his tent, his memorial shall not be found] (cf. Job 28:21).
The life of the criminal is a dream. No, even the very rest of the wicked while they live here is an illusion; they are in hell now, since they go down into Gehenna while they are alive [3].
v St. Job answers: Do not think that you are happy while you are immersed in pleasures, because the blows of God have not fallen upon you in this life.
“The lamp of the wicked is put out.” It gives light for a time, but it does not carry an eternal light.

And although the world favors such people, because they carry out the will of God who has authority over the world (Jn 14:30), yet usually a moment of reversal in events comes, when sorrows come from the wrath and indignation of heaven, when the wicked are sifted “as stubble before the wind.” The unjust are sifted like chaff, and the righteous like wheat. Turn to the Lord who said to Peter: “Behold, Satan hath desired to have you, that he may sift you as wheat: but I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not” (Lk 22:31-32) [4].

St. Ambrose v “And the number of the years of his oppression is uncertain”… It is known that every proud man exercises tyranny according to his measure. One exercises it in a state, by virtue of his high position that suits him; another in a province, another in a city, another in his household, and another hides his evil and exercises it upon himself in the thought of his heart.

For God is not concerned with the quantity of evil that a man is able to practice, but with the quantity that is in his mind to practice. And when a man has no authority outwardly, he is counted a tyrant inwardly, and iniquity rules over him within. For although he does not oppress his relatives outwardly, inwardly he seeks to find an opportunity and authority to oppress others. For God looks into the hearts of men, and in the eyes of God the wicked man is counted as having actually done what he imagines.
Pope Gregory (the Great)

entries.section: 6. Joash the son of Ahaziah hidden in the temple

paragraphs.text: 11 But Jehoshabeath, the daughter of the king, took Joash the son of Ahaziah, and stole him from among the king’s sons that were slain, and put him and his nurse in a bedchamber. So Jehoshabeath, the daughter of king Jehoram, the wife of Jehoiada the priest, (for she was the sister of Ahaziah,) hid him from Athaliah, so that she slew him not. 12 And he was with them hid in the house of God six years: and Athaliah reigned over the land.

But Jehoshabeath, the daughter of the king, took Joash the son of Ahaziah, and stole him from among the king’s sons that were slain, and put him and his nurse in a bedchamber. So Jehoshabeath, the daughter of king Jehoram, the wife of Jehoiada the priest,
(for she was the sister of Ahaziah,)
hid him from Athaliah, so that she slew him not. [11]
Ahaziah trusted in his mother Athaliah the daughter of Omri, an extremely violent woman, who counselled him to do evil [3]. He made an alliance with Jehoram the son of Ahab.

In the midst of the massacre that Athaliah carried out to destroy all the royal seed so that she alone might remain in power, the lamp of the Lord’s anointed was not put out; for God preserved a weak infant, as a symbol of the Lord Christ, who was preserved from the massacre of the children of Bethlehem.

In the sabbatical year, the seventh year, the year of the land’s rest, Joash appeared to reign before the eyes of all; it was declared that he was the only king who had the authority to wear the crown.
v Just as what God has prepared for those who love Him surpasses the mind, so also the torments He has prepared for the wicked surpass the mind [5].

Origen v The wicked are scattered bitterly (like light tares), but the righteous are saved like heavy wheat. Notice what the Lord says to Peter: “Behold, Satan hath desired to have you, that he may sift you as wheat: but I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not” (Lk 22:31-32). Those who are scattered like tares perish, but he who does not perish is like the seed that falls and grows and increases and brings forth much fruit (Lk 8:8)… Evil is likened to the chaff that burns quickly and turns to dust [6].
St. Ambrose

entries.section: 6. Joash the son of Ahaziah hidden in the temple

paragraphs.text: And he was with them hid in the house of God six years: and Athaliah reigned over the land. [12]

Her love of shedding blood made her lose her popularity, if she ever had any. Her taking the throne had no legal basis whatever. All that characterized her was her violence and tyranny, and she thought that no one could disobey her or resist her.

The hiding of the child in the house of God came by surpassing divine wisdom: 1. It was not possible for any man to hide the child in his house, lest the news leak out and Athaliah take vengeance on the owner of the house and all his family. 2. The remaining of a little child with his nurse in the house of the Lord for six years without the news leaking out to the queen did not happen in vain, but by a divine plan that reveals God’s own care for the matter. 3. The keeping of the child in the house of the Lord under the care of the high priest revealed the plan of God, who assigned a certain tribe to the priestly work and another to the kingly work, with the cooperation of the two tribes. It is as though God declares His care for His people spiritually and temporally.
Grant me the spirit of care and leadership
v Grant me Your Spirit working in me, O Good Shepherd.
In Your love You shepherd Your people, and You lay down Yourself for them.
In Your love You raise up from every child a loving leader!
v Ahaziah took the throne, and he had no sincere principles.
His wicked mother led him and counselled him with her evil.
She drove him to evil, and deprived him of clinging to You.
She drove him to cling to Jehoram the idolater.
He thought that in his alliance with Jehoram his soul would be at ease.
But behold, death pursued him, and shame clung to him.
v Athaliah, his mother, took the throne of her son.
In her love of power, she killed every male of the house of David.
She killed and rested, and thought that she was in safety and stability.
There was no longer anyone to rival her for her throne.
There was no one who could stand before her.
And in the whole kingdom there was no one who could disobey her.
She remained on the throne six years, and thought that she was mighty and wise and a unique leader.
No one of the house of David was sitting on the throne any longer.
And the prophecies concerning the house of David could not be fulfilled.
v But You, O Good Shepherd, rescued a child one year old.
You embraced him in Your holy temple.
You guarded him with Your care, and prepared him to sit on the throne.
You work through the many as through the few, and through the great as through the little child.
You pour out Your Spirit upon Your believers, and they bear the spirit of love, care and leadership!

entries.section: 1. Jehoiada prepares the people to receive Joash

paragraphs.text: 1 And in the seventh year Jehoiada strengthened himself, and took the captains of hundreds, Azariah the son of Jeroham, and Ishmael the son of Jehohanan, and Azariah the son of Obed, and Maaseiah the son of Adaiah, and Elishaphat the son of Zichri, into covenant with him. 2 And they went about in Judah, and gathered the Levites out of all the cities of Judah, and the chief of the fathers of Israel, and they came to Jerusalem. 3 And all the congregation made a covenant with the king in the house of God. And he said unto them, Behold, the king’s son shall reign, as the LORD hath said of the sons of David. 4 This is the thing that ye shall do; A third part of you entering on the sabbath, of the priests and of the Levites, shall be porters of the doors; 5 And a third part shall be at the king’s house; and a third part at the gate of the foundation: and all the people shall be in the courts of the house of the LORD. 6 But let none come into the house of the LORD, save the priests, and they that minister of the Levites; they shall go in, for they are holy: but all the people shall keep the watch of the LORD. 7 And the Levites shall compass the king round about, every man with his weapons in his hand; and whosoever else cometh into the house, he shall be put to death: but be ye with the king when he cometh in, and when he goeth out. 8 So the Levites and all Judah did according to all things that Jehoiada the priest had commanded, and took every man his men that were to come in on the sabbath, with them that were to go out on the sabbath: for Jehoiada the priest dismissed not the courses. 9 Moreover Jehoiada the priest delivered to the captains of hundreds spears, and bucklers, and shields, that had been king David’s, which were in the house of God. 10 And he set all the people, every man having his weapon in his hand, from the right side of the temple to the left side of the temple, along by the altar and the temple, by the king round about.
And in the seventh year Jehoiada strengthened himself, and took the captains of hundreds into covenant with him,
Azariah the son of Jeroham, and Ishmael the son of Jehohanan, and Azariah the son of Obed, and Maaseiah the son of Adaiah, and Elishaphat the son of Zichri [1]

The Book of Kings did not mention the names of these captains of hundreds. It only mentioned the existence of royal guards in five divisions (2 Kgs 11:4-8). The five captains of hundreds belonged to the royal guard, and they were displeased with Athaliah and her attitudes of hostility toward the house of the Lord and toward the seed of David, and they were probably on friendly terms with Jehoiada the priest.

The character of the priest Jehoiada Jehoiada is regarded as an ideal priest who served not for his own sake or for the people’s, but for the glory of God; it befits us to imitate him in many matters.

a. He was a man of wisdom, good management and a holy life. He preserved the little prince for several years until he became able to appear before the people and the good leaders who were weary of the conduct of the queen who had usurped the throne. Jehoiada planned this work and carried it out with wonderful secrecy and speed, without slackness.

v He presented three marks of preaching the Word: a burning, venturesome zeal; a soul ready to endure whatever dangers might befall; and knowledge and wisdom joined together. For his love of venture in his preaching, and in his blameless life, would have profited him nothing had he not received the power of the Spirit. Look at him as he appears first in himself, or rather hear his words: [that our ministry be not blamed](*) [1].

entries.section: 1. Jehoiada prepares the people to receive Joash

paragraphs.text: v It befits the priest to shine, giving light by his good conduct to all people, that they may imitate his example. But if this light turns into darkness, what will become of the world?! Will it not become a ruin? [2]
St. John Chrysostom b. A man of God, he feels that God has called him to this work and accompanies him in his work, and without Him he cannot carry out his priestly work.
v Who is pure and without falsehood before God, that he may put on fire, and rise and serve the flame?
What earthly man has been set aflame by Your divinity so that he is able to hold that incomprehensible flame?
Who has been purified from the filth of the hateful world, and has risen to a degree of great glory, that he may serve as priest?

entries.section: 1. Jehoiada prepares the people to receive Joash

paragraphs.text: Were anyone a fiery seraph, he would not be able to minister as priest the sacrifices of the rank of the perfect apostles [3].

St. Jacob of Serugh c. A man of influence and attraction, to whom the commanders joined themselves, and the Levites and the chief of the fathers of Israel submitted when he called them to Jerusalem [2]. As a wise and loving man who had been given authority by God, they listen to him quietly (Eccl 9:17).

entries.section: 1. Jehoiada prepares the people to receive Joash

paragraphs.text: v As a king sends out governors, giving them authority to cast into prison or to bring out of it, so when He sent them out He endowed them with the same authority [4].

St. John Chrysostom d. A man of great faith, those around him did not move him, but the Word of God led him, and he sought to act according to the will of God [3]. He acted not merely to make the king’s young son reign in order to resist Athaliah, but “as the LORD hath said” [3].

v It is a severe judgment under which those who teach fall. This is what the disciple of Christ shows, who says: “My brethren, be not many masters, knowing that we shall receive the greater condemnation” (Jas 3:1). For the gift of spiritual graces is abundant for those who are the leaders of the people, since the wise Paul writes to the blessed Timothy: “and the Lord give thee understanding in all things” (2 Tim 2:7), [neglect not also the gift of God that is in thee by the putting on of my hands] (cf. 2 Tim 1:6). From this it is evident that the Saviour of all, in giving them more, demands more of them.

entries.section: 1. Jehoiada prepares the people to receive Joash

paragraphs.text: What are the virtues He demands of them? Steadfastness in the faith, sound teaching, being well established in hope, unshaken patience, unconquerable spiritual strength, and joy and courage in every good advance. By this we become an example to others in the life of the Gospel. If we live thus, Christ grants us the crown, through whom and with whom be praise and dominion to the Father and the Holy Spirit forever and ever, Amen [5].
St. Cyril the Great e. A man of worship, not for carrying out rites without understanding, but seeking God through it and in it. He finds his fullness in God.

entries.section: 1. Jehoiada prepares the people to receive Joash

paragraphs.text: v The perfect servant of Christ has nothing besides Christ [6].
St. Jerome f. A man of strong will and wonderful determination. He exposed himself to being killed, but he acted in the spirit of power without fear.
v He who has disciplined his desires and trained his soul to endure, and has grown to a state of perfect knowledge, is equal to the angels!

He has indeed been enlightened and has become shining as the sun in the practice of kindness, hastening with a knowledge full of righteousness to the holy tabernacle through the love of God, as the apostles did. For these apostles did not become apostles because they were chosen for the apostleship on account of a privilege in their nature, since Judas also was chosen from among them, but they were able to be apostles (to practice the enlightened apostolic life)… so that they might see unlimited things. Matthias was not chosen among them, but he showed himself worthy to be an apostle in place of Judas.

entries.section: 1. Jehoiada prepares the people to receive Joash

paragraphs.text: Now also, he who trains himself in the commandments of the Lord, and lives in perfection with knowledge according to the Gospel, is counted in the body of the chosen apostles. Such a one is truly a priest of the Church, and a true servant (deacon) of the will of God, so long as he works and teaches according to the Lord, and not merely because he was ordained by men; he is not counted righteous merely because he is a priest, but has come to be in the priesthood because he is righteous. For even if he does not receive here on earth the honor of the greatest seat, yet he will sit (with) the twenty-four thrones, judging men, as John said in the Book of Revelation [7].
St. Clement of Alexandria

entries.section: 1. Jehoiada prepares the people to receive Joash

paragraphs.text: And they went about in Judah, and gathered the Levites out of all the cities of Judah, and the chief of the fathers of Israel, and they came to Jerusalem. [2]

Jehoiada was careful to call the military leaders together with the civil and religious ones to carry out the revolt against Athaliah and to proclaim Joash king. The captains of hundreds moved and gathered the religious leaders (the Levites) and the political leaders (the chief of the fathers of Israel), so that all might assemble together in Jerusalem.
By Israel here is meant the kingdom of Judah, which included Judah and Benjamin and the pious of the other tribes, who had left the northern kingdom and joined the southern kingdom.

The priest Jehoiada did not summon the heads of the tribes in the northern kingdom, because they could not be trusted with a matter like this, for they had abandoned the temple and accepted the limiting of kings to the seed of David.

It is probable that what happened took place during the celebration of one of the great annual feasts, when the Jews gathered in Jerusalem. Thus Athaliah did not sense that a plot had been prepared against her.

entries.section: 1. Jehoiada prepares the people to receive Joash

paragraphs.text: And all the congregation made a covenant with the king in the house of God.
And he said unto them, Behold, the king’s son shall reign, as the LORD hath said of the sons of David. [3]
By all the congregation here he meant the leaders mentioned in the preceding passage.

entries.section: 1. Jehoiada prepares the people to receive Joash

paragraphs.text: This is the thing that ye shall do;
A third part of you entering on the sabbath, of the priests and of the Levites, shall be porters of the doors; [4]

Jehoiada, in his wisdom and his desire for collective work, gathered the military, religious and civil leaders, so that all might feel that the work belonged to everyone and not to a particular group; yet he was careful to have the priests and Levites rally around the king, and to observe the Law concerning the celebration in the temple.

entries.section: 1. Jehoiada prepares the people to receive Joash

paragraphs.text: “This is the thing that ye shall do”: here he describes the organization for defending this revolt against Athaliah and enthroning Joash as king. He divided those carrying out the guard into three groups: one section to guard the king wherever he was [7], and two sections to guard all the doors and entrances of the house of the Lord and of the king’s house.

entries.section: 1. Jehoiada prepares the people to receive Joash

paragraphs.text: And a third part shall be at the king’s house; and a third part at the gate of the foundation: and all the people shall be in the courts of the house of the LORD. [5]

paragraphs.text: But let none come into the house of the LORD, save the priests, and they that minister of the Levites; they shall go in, for they are holy: but all the people shall keep the watch of the LORD. [6]

paragraphs.text: And the Levites shall compass the king round about, every man with his weapons in his hand;
and whosoever else cometh into the house, he shall be put to death:
but be ye with the king when he cometh in, and when he goeth out. [7]
Jehoiada probably feared an attack by the priests of Baal upon the king inside the temple; therefore the Levites surrounding the king carried weapons to prevent them from entering.

entries.section: 1. Jehoiada prepares the people to receive Joash

paragraphs.text: So the Levites and all Judah did according to all things that Jehoiada the priest had commanded,
and took every man his men that were to come in on the sabbath, with them that were to go out on the sabbath: for Jehoiada the priest dismissed not the courses. [8]

The priests and Levites were divided into courses, each course taking its turn and departing so that another course might take its place. But in this event Jehoiada considered all the courses to be in a state of emergency, so he did not allow them to depart until the celebration was completed and he was assured that calm and peace prevailed throughout the city.

paragraphs.text: And he set all the people, every man having his weapon in his hand, from the right side of the temple to the left side of the temple, along by the altar and the temple, by the king round about. [10]

entries.section: 2. Jehoiada shows the king to the people

paragraphs.text: Then they brought out the king’s son, and put upon him the crown, and gave him the testimony, and made him king.
And Jehoiada and his sons anointed him, and said, God save the king. [11]

How great was the joy of the people as they saw the little child, the son of David, standing on the platform. The despair that had come upon the majority was shattered, and they ran rejoicing to see what they had not expected.

The Targum says: [And they brought the king’s son, and put upon him the royal crown that David had taken from the head of the king of the children of Ammon. It was set with an attractive precious stone, and there was engraved on it what expresses the greatness and honor of the name “Yahweh,” which he had placed upon him by the Holy Spirit. It weighed a talent of gold. This was a testimony to the house of David, and that a king who was not of the house of David could not bear its weight. And when the people saw that it had been placed on the head of Joash and that he bore this crown, they believed that he was of the seed of David, and immediately they made him king. Then Jehoiada and his sons anointed him, and said: May the king prosper in his kingdom!]

When David killed Goliath, he took the crown that was on his head and the bracelet that was on his arm, and presented them to King Saul (2 Sam 1:10). As for the testimony that was given to the king, it is said to be a scroll on which the Law was written (Deut 17:18), placed in the hands of the king who holds the scepter of the kingdom.
The king would receive this scroll in his hands and place it above his head before reading it, as a sign of his submission to what was in the scroll and his honoring of what was written in it.

entries.section: 3. The killing of Athaliah, the usurper of the throne

paragraphs.text: 12 Now when Athaliah heard the noise of the people running and praising the king, she came to the people into the house of the LORD: 13 And she looked, and, behold, the king stood at his pillar at the entering in, and the princes and the trumpets by the king: and all the people of the land rejoiced, and sounded with trumpets, also the singers with instruments of musick, and such as taught to sing praise. Then Athaliah rent her clothes, and said, Treason, Treason. 14 Then Jehoiada the priest brought out the captains of hundreds that were set over the host, and said unto them, Have her forth of the ranges: and whoso followeth her, let him be slain with the sword. For the priest said, Slay her not in the house of the LORD. 15 So they laid hands on her; and when she was come to the entering of the horse gate by the king’s house, they slew her there.
Now when Athaliah heard the noise of the people running and praising the king, she came to the people into the house of the LORD. [12]
Queen Athaliah dared to enter the temple, thinking that her influence could be stopped by nothing.

entries.section: 3. The killing of Athaliah, the usurper of the throne

paragraphs.text: And she looked, and, behold, the king stood at his pillar at the entering in, and the princes and the trumpets by the king: and all the people of the land rejoiced, and sounded with trumpets, also the singers with instruments of musick, and such as taught to sing praise.
Then Athaliah rent her clothes, and said, Treason, Treason. [13]

The king was on his stand in the court of the people, opposite the priests, for the little king had been brought from the inside to the court of the people. Some see that the king was on the bronze platform of Solomon, placed beside the stand (the pillar).
Athaliah did not think that anyone of the house of David had escaped the massacre she had committed. Suddenly she saw what she had not reckoned on, and she cried out: “Treason! Treason!”

It befits the righteous not to gloat over the wicked at their destruction, for they carry the will of their Father that all people be saved and come to the knowledge of the truth (1 Tim 2:4); but they rejoice in the destruction of the authority of evil and injustice, lest the weak stumble, as they also are glad at the glory of God, which does not admit corruption.

The righteous find the opportunity to reveal the futility of evil, its weakness and its impermanence, and the folly of the wisdom of the wicked, their cunning and their malice. The righteous are glad at the collapse of the devil and his kingdom, and at the destruction of sin, not of the sinner. For the righteous man knows nothing but love, even toward sinners.

entries.section: 3. The killing of Athaliah, the usurper of the throne

paragraphs.text: v [The righteous see it, and are glad: and the innocent laugh them to scorn](**) [19]. When the righteous see the wicked sinning here, they are not glad at the error of people who destroy themselves. For if they were glad at error, they would no longer be counted righteous…

The Pharisee lost his righteousness because he was glad, counting himself higher than the tax collector, saying: “I thank thee, that I am not as other men are, extortioners, unjust, adulterers, or even as this publican” (Lk 18:11).

Again, if we say that the righteous man can triumph with complete joy at the death of the wicked, what kind of joy is this, for vengeance on the wicked in this world, in which the life of the righteous man is uncertain?

Let us distinguish between the times of terror and the times of glory. The righteous now see the wicked, and they grow lean on account of their evils. And when they see them struck, they do not trust in their own lives either (***)… Now the righteous see the sons of perdition and groan, and at the final judgment they will see them and laugh them to scorn.
Pope Gregory (the Great)

entries.section: 3. The killing of Athaliah, the usurper of the throne

paragraphs.text: Then Jehoiada the priest brought out the captains of hundreds that were set over the host, and said unto them,
Have her forth of the ranges: and whoso followeth her, let him be slain with the sword.
For the priest said, Slay her not in the house of the LORD. [14]

With wisdom Jehoiada took every precaution that the wicked woman not be killed in the house of the Lord, for the place is holy and no disgrace must touch it. At the same time the tyrant queen must not be left, lest she assassinate the little king; therefore he ordered the killing of whoever followed her, refusing to set up Joash as king.

entries.section: 3. The killing of Athaliah, the usurper of the throne

paragraphs.text: So they laid hands on her;
and when she was come to the entering of the horse gate by the king’s house, they slew her there. [15]
v Those who consent to iniquity will have no portion among the immortals [8].

St. Antony the Great v “Thou hast put out their name for ever and ever” (Ps 9:5). You destroy them utterly, you uproot them from their roots, and you blot them out, so that even their memory disappears… [Their memory perished with a crash] (Job 18:18). And in another text, “their memorial is perished with them.” What does he mean by saying “with a crash”? He speaks of a complete destruction, or of the hideousness of evils. And this is in fact a sign of God’s providence, that He does not do this in secret, so that He may correct the condition of men through the calamities of others. Therefore he points to the desire for the destruction that comes upon them [9].

St. John Chrysostom v This chaff does not destroy those who are the wheat of the Lord, who are few if compared with the others, yet they are a great multitude. The elect of God, who are gathered from the ends of the world, from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other (Mt 24:31), do not perish. The elect cry out, saying: “Save, LORD; for the godly man ceaseth; for the faithful fail from among the children of men” (Ps 12:1). And the Lord says to them: [He that shall endure unto the end (where evil is bound), the same shall be saved] (Mt 24:13) [10].

v “The earth shook and trembled” (Ps 18:7). When the Son of Man was glorified thus, sinners shook and trembled. “The foundations also of the hills trembled” (Ps 18:7), for the hope of the proud who were in this life trembled. “And [they] were shaken because he was wroth.” This is the hope in temporal blessings, no longer established in the hearts of men [11].
St. Augustine v “The hills melted like wax” (Ps 97:5). To me the hills seem to be the powers of the demons. Whether they are hills or not, they are certainly the proud men.
This fire does not destroy those below (the humble), but destroys only the haughty.
As a matter of fact, lightning rarely affects those who are in the valley, but those who are on high, on the hills, will not escape it.
St. Jerome Josephus sees that she was killed at the gate of the mules, southeast of the temple, near the horse gate in the Kidron valley, which at that time was counted an unclean place [12].

entries.section: 4. The reforms of the king

paragraphs.text: 16 And Jehoiada made a covenant between him, and between all the people, and between the king, that they should be the LORD’s people. 17 Then all the people went to the house of Baal, and brake it down, and brake his altars and his images in pieces, and slew Mattan the priest of Baal before the altars. 18 Also Jehoiada appointed the offices of the house of the LORD by the hand of the priests the Levites, whom David had distributed in the house of the LORD, to offer the burnt offerings of the LORD, as it is written in the law of Moses, with rejoicing and with singing, as it was ordained by David. 19 And he set the porters at the gates of the house of the LORD, that none which was unclean in any thing should enter in. 20 And he took the captains of hundreds, and the nobles, and the governors of the people, and all the people of the land, and brought down the king from the house of the LORD: and they came through the high gate into the king’s house, and set the king upon the throne of the kingdom. 21 And all the people of the land rejoiced: and the city was quiet, after that they had slain Athaliah with the sword.
And Jehoiada made a covenant between him, and between all the people, and between the king, that they should be the LORD’s people. [16]

Jehoiada was careful to begin the reform by renewing the covenant with God. He made a covenant between himself, as the representative of God, and the people and the king, after Athaliah had corrupted the worship of God and had done all she could to replace the worship of God with the worship of idols.

A threefold covenant: the priest was careful to renew the compact between the Lord and the king, between God and the people, and between the king and the people (2 Kgs 11:17). As for the aim of this renewal of the covenant, it was the concern that the people be “the LORD’s people,” so that neither king nor priest nor people would seek glory for themselves but for the Lord.

entries.section: 4. The reforms of the king

paragraphs.text: Then all the people went to the house of Baal, and brake it down, and brake his altars and his images in pieces, and slew Mattan the priest of Baal before the altars. [17]
The most hideous thing Athaliah did was to walk in the way of her wicked mother Jezebel, and to introduce the worship of Baal and support it.
The Law demanded the killing of the priests of idols, because they seduce the people to idol worship and its abominations (Deut 7:5-6).

Mattan: probably the first priest of Baal, who came accompanying Athaliah from Samaria, and was the one close to Jeroboam in spreading the worship of Baal in Jerusalem; Josephus called him Mathan [13].

entries.section: 4. The reforms of the king

paragraphs.text: The temple was neglected in the days of the wicked kings, and there occurred a mixing of the worship of God with the worship of idols, and the order of the temple was corrupted; therefore Jehoiada the high priest did the following: 1. He appointed the priests to offer the burnt offerings as it is written in the law of Moses. 2. He appointed the singers according to the order of David the prophet and king, since worship was bound up with joy (Rom 5:11). 3. He set the keepers of the gates as David had commanded [19], so that no one who was unclean might enter the temple.

entries.section: 4. The reforms of the king

paragraphs.text: And all the people of the land rejoiced: and the city was quiet, after that they had slain Athaliah with the sword. [21]

What is noticed in all these reforms is the dominance of the spirit of true joy with inner peace. Thus when the Son of David reigns over the heart, the joy of the Spirit does not depart from us, and we enjoy the pledge of heaven!
Reign in my heart, and kill every evil in it!
v Athaliah thought that she had become queen, and she killed every heir to the throne.
By her tyranny she moved the leaders like chess pieces.
She thought that there was no God whom she should fear!
v She found her pleasures in the worship of Baal, and set herself up as a goddess whom no one could withstand.
She made light of all Your promises to the house of David.
She planned, and thought it impossible that the house of David should have a place on the throne.
v Your providence is wonderful, and Your plans are wise.
You moved Your priest Jehoiada and his wife to preserve a child who seemed forgotten.
And the time came for him to sit on the seat of the throne.
With joy the military, religious and civil leaders moved.
Athaliah was killed at the gate of the mules, and with her was killed Mattan, the priest of Baal.
v You became incarnate, O Word of God, and became a child, and You terrified the devil and all his powers.
You are enthroned upon the hearts of men, and You establish Your Kingdom within them.
You transform those of dust into the likeness of heavenly beings.
And You join men to the heavenly choir.
To You be glory, O Saviour of mankind.
